correctness.rationale: The center classification is exhaustive for metric-star partial injections. Distinct nilpotent center-moving patterns have counts 2m and m(m-1), while the leaf-only sector is exactly a labeled set of directed paths. The bivariate EGF follows from labeled exponential enumeration, and binomial-rank totals follow from concatenating and cutting paths. The conditional-Poisson construction proves the Gumbel law, using a Fourier local central limit bound with variance asymptotic to 2m^(3/2); an added geometric size variable proves density asymptotic to 1/(2 sqrt(m)). The standalone checker directly enumerated all partial isometries for m=1..5 and reproduced every joint count (VERIFY_OK). Finite checks alone would not prove the asymptotic claims.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A nilpotent partial injection is a set of directed paths, and its unrestricted chain enumeration is prior work. A star-metric partial isometry is a strict subset of partial injections: it permits only 2m center-moving singleton arrows and m(m-1) nilpotent center-through chains, forbidding all other center-containing nilpotents. The full rank-index formula and extreme-value asymptotics concern the constrained monoid, not the symmetric inverse semigroup. Complete pre-existing full texts could not be inspected, so equivalence risk remains.

value.rationale: Rank and nilpotency index jointly stratify the entire natural transformation monoid, rather than describing an ad hoc finite slice. The complete formula distinguishes center-moving bounded-index behavior from leaf-supported nilpotents, gives the exact nilpotent density to leading order, and proves a nondegenerate Gumbel law for the typical index. The conditional-Poisson local limit and all-rank exact formulas give reusable quantitative descriptions. The result does not claim any broad theorem about arbitrary graph isometries.
